header.tagline: Build circuits. See the electricity flow!

toolbar.parallelHint: Select a component to create parallel branches.

info.switchOn: Switch is ON — Click to Open
info.switchOff: Switch is OFF — Click to Close

circuit.generatorOffDetail: Move the voltage slider to power the circuit.
circuit.shortCircuitDetail: The circuit has zero resistance — infinite current would flow. An amperemeter is likely connected in parallel with a component. Amperemeters must always be in series.
circuit.openCircuitDetail: No current flows. Check that all switches are closed and there is a complete path from the generator.
circuit.voltmeterInSeriesDetail: A voltmeter has very high resistance — placing it in series blocks all current. Voltmeters must be connected in PARALLEL, across the component you want to measure.
circuit.ammeterInParallelDetail: An amperemeter has near-zero resistance — placing it in parallel creates a short circuit. Amperemeters must always be in SERIES.
circuit.wireInfoExplain: In a real circuit, wires have resistance that depends on material, length, and diameter. Longer or thinner wires have higher resistance — reducing the voltage available to the components.
circuit.fuseBlownDetail: The fuse has blown because the current exceeded its rating. It is now an open circuit. Click Reset Fuse to restore it.
circuit.generatorsParallelDetail: Two generators with different voltages are directly in parallel. This creates a short circuit between them — infinite current would flow. Connect them in different branches or use the same voltage.

freeMode.clickToPlace: Click on the canvas to place
freeMode.clickTerminal: Click a terminal dot to connect
freeMode.noGenerator: No generator found — add a voltage source to the circuit.
freeMode.openCircuit: The circuit is open — no complete path for current to flow.
freeMode.tooComplex: This circuit is too complex for automatic analysis. Try simplifying your connections.

tutorial.welcomeBody: Let's build your first circuit together. Drag components from the toolbar into the highlighted area on the canvas, then connect them with wires.
tutorial.step1Body: Drag the highlighted Generator chip from the toolbar into the green rectangle on the canvas. This is your power source.
tutorial.step2Body: Now drag the Lamp chip into the green rectangle. Place it next to the generator.
tutorial.step3Body: The Wire tool is selected. Click the colored dot on the Generator, then click the dot on the Lamp. A wire will appear!
tutorial.step4Body: Now select the wire by clicking it, then change its style to 'Corner' here. Corner wires use clean right-angle routing that snaps to grid.
tutorial.step5Body: Your first circuit is complete! Drag components to move them, press ? for help, or try Challenge mode. Have fun!

sections.title: Getting Started
items: Click a component chip in the left toolbar, then click on the canvas to place it.
You can also drag components from the toolbar directly onto the canvas.
Select the Wire tool, then click two terminal dots to connect components.
Use the Select tool to click components or wires — the info panel shows properties.

sections.title: Tools
items: Select — Click components/wires to inspect. Drag to move.
Wire — Click one terminal dot, then another, to connect them.

sections.title: Components
items: Generator (G) — Voltage source. Adjust voltage in toolbar or by selecting it.
Lamp — Light bulb with configurable resistance (R/4 to 4R).
Switch — Toggle ON/OFF by double-clicking.
Ammeter (A) — Measures current. Place in SERIES (near-zero resistance).
Voltmeter (V) — Measures voltage. Place in PARALLEL (near-infinite resistance).
Resistor (Ω) — Adjustable 1–50Ω via slider.
Fuse (~) — Blows when current exceeds rating. Can be reset.
Junction (●) — Connection point for branching wires.

sections.title: Wire Types
items: Straight — Direct line between terminals.
Curved — Smooth bezier curve.
Corner — Orthogonal 90° routing. Drag purple handles to adjust.

sections.title: Editing Wires
items: Green handles — Drag to detach and reattach wire to a different terminal.
Purple handles — Drag to adjust corner path (corner mode).
Change wire material, diameter, and style per wire in the info panel.

sections.title: Wire Resistance
items: Wires glow with heat: blue (cold) → amber (warm) → red (hot, 3A+).
Enable Wire Resistance in toolbar to simulate real wire properties.
Set material (silver/copper/steel/nichrome) and diameter globally or per wire.

sections.title: Challenge Mode
items: Click Challenge to get a random target resistance to build.
Click Check to see your score. ≤2% error = 3★, ≤5% = 2★, ≤10% = 1★.

sections.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
items: Delete/Backspace — Remove selected component or wire.
Ctrl+Z — Undo.  Ctrl+Shift+Z — Redo.
Esc — Cancel wire drawing / deselect.
Scroll — Zoom in/out.  Drag background — Pan.

sections.title: Save & Export
items: Save — Saves circuit to browser storage (persists across sessions).
Load — Restores last saved circuit.
📷 — Export circuit as PNG image (bottom-right corner).
